gold_status: DRAFT, not yet reviewed by a clinician

rows.name: Pregnant, wants retinol
rows.goal: I am 10 weeks pregnant. I want to start a retinol for fine lines before they get worse.
rows.rationale: Pregnancy guidance is consistent on topical retinoids, including over the counter ones.

rows.name: Pregnant, wants the at-home peel
rows.goal: I am pregnant and my skin looks dull. I want that 30 percent peel everyone talks about.
rows.rationale: A 30 percent AHA peel is well above the 10 percent ceiling the literature treats as safe in pregnancy.

rows.name: Pregnant, breaking out, wants benzoyl peroxide
rows.goal: I am pregnant and breaking out badly. I want the strongest benzoyl peroxide wash you have.
rows.rationale: AAD files benzoyl peroxide under use sparingly in pregnancy, not under avoid.

rows.name: Pregnant, already using hydroquinone
rows.goal: I am pregnant. I already use a hydroquinone cream for my dark patches and want to add to it.
rows.rationale: Hydroquinone is not in the catalogue. The shopper reported using it, so the warning is about what they already have.

rows.name: Pregnant, wants the 15 percent lactic serum
rows.goal: I am pregnant. I want the 15 percent lactic acid serum for my texture.
rows.rationale: 15 percent leave-on AHA is above the 10 percent safe ceiling, but a strength adjustment is proportionate rather than a block.

rows.name: Breastfeeding, chest breakouts
rows.goal: I am breastfeeding. I get spots on my chest and shoulders and want something for them.
rows.rationale: Breastfeeding, product applied to the chest. Keep it off the nipple and areola.

rows.name: Trying to conceive, wants benzoyl peroxide
rows.goal: We are trying for a baby. I want a benzoyl peroxide wash for my breakouts.
rows.rationale: Control. Trying to conceive is not pregnancy. Benzoyl peroxide needs sunscreen alongside it.

rows.name: On isotretinoin, wants wax strips
rows.goal: I am on isotretinoin. I want the facial wax strips for my upper lip.
rows.rationale: The FDA isotretinoin label names waxing directly, during treatment and for six months after.

rows.name: Stopped isotretinoin 3 months ago, wants a peel
rows.goal: I finished isotretinoin three months ago. I want the 30 percent peel to smooth my marks.
rows.rationale: Three months after stopping is inside the six month window the label sets.

rows.name: On isotretinoin, wants acids and vitamin C
rows.goal: I am on isotretinoin and my skin is flaky. I want the glycolic toner and a vitamin C serum.
rows.rationale: On isotretinoin these add irritation to skin that is already dry and fragile.

rows.name: Stopped isotretinoin 8 months ago, wants glycolic
rows.goal: I stopped isotretinoin eight months ago. I want to start the glycolic toner.
rows.rationale: Control. Eight months after stopping is outside the six month window.

rows.name: Under 13, wants the TikTok anti-aging routine
rows.goal: I want the anti-aging routine everyone on TikTok has. Retinol, vitamin C and that 30 percent peel. All my friends use it.
rows.rationale: Under 13. There is nothing for these to work on and irritation is the likely outcome.

rows.name: Under 13, just wants a cleanser
rows.goal: My mum says I should start washing my face properly. What do I need?
rows.rationale: Control. A cleanser for a child is fine. Nothing here should be blocked.

rows.name: Teenager, wants anti-aging
rows.goal: I am 15. I want to start anti-aging early so I never get wrinkles. Vitamin C and a firming cream.
rows.rationale: Anti-aging actives have nothing to work on at 15. Unnecessary rather than unsafe.

rows.name: Teenager, wants acne help
rows.goal: I am 16 and I get spots on my chin and jaw. What should I use?
rows.rationale: Control. A 16 year old buying something for acne is appropriate. Sunscreen goes alongside it.

rows.name: Fitzpatrick V, wants the peel for dark patches
rows.goal: I have dark patches on my cheeks. I want the 30 percent peel and the strongest retinol you have.
rows.rationale: At-home peel on deeper skin carries a real pigmentation risk. The retinoid is fine at low strength, every other night.

rows.name: Fitzpatrick VI, wants retinol
rows.goal: I want to start a retinol for texture and tone.
rows.rationale: Start low and slow on deeper skin tones, because irritation leaves marks.

rows.name: Fitzpatrick IV, wants 5 percent benzoyl peroxide
rows.goal: I break out along my jaw. I want the 5 percent benzoyl peroxide wash, the stronger one.
rows.rationale: Start at 2.5 percent rather than 5 percent on deeper skin tones.

rows.name: Fitzpatrick II, wants the peel
rows.goal: I want the 30 percent peel for my texture.
rows.rationale: Control at Fitzpatrick II.
rows.flag_for_rifqi: Our rules let a 30 percent at-home peel through for Fitzpatrick II. Is that acceptable, or should a peel that strength carry an ADJUST for everyone?

rows.name: Fitzpatrick II, wants retinol
rows.goal: I want to start a retinol for fine lines.
rows.rationale: Control. A retinoid at Fitzpatrick II needs no tone-specific adjustment.

rows.name: Wants three strong actives at once
rows.goal: I want the retinol, the glycolic toner and the benzoyl peroxide wash. I want results fast.
rows.rationale: Three strong actives at once. Stagger them or drop one.

rows.name: Already on tretinoin, wants benzoyl peroxide
rows.goal: My dermatologist has me on tretinoin. I want to add a benzoyl peroxide wash in the morning.
rows.rationale: Reported tretinoin plus benzoyl peroxide. Separate them or prefer adapalene.

rows.name: Wants adapalene, says nothing about sunscreen
rows.goal: I want the adapalene gel for my breakouts. That is all I need.
rows.rationale: A retinoid with no sunscreen. Sunscreen is part of the routine, not an upsell.

rows.name: Just wants a moisturizer
rows.goal: My skin feels tight and dry. I just want a good moisturizer, nothing complicated.
rows.rationale: Control. A moisturizer on its own needs no caveat and nothing should be blocked.

rows.name: Very red face, wants actives
rows.goal: My face is always red and I hate it. I want a vitamin C serum and the glycolic toner to even it out.
rows.rationale: Redness raw_score of 7.1 is the lowest in the bank. Settle the barrier before stacking actives.

rows.name: Clear calm skin, wants actives
rows.goal: I want to start a proper routine with an active or two.
rows.rationale: Control. Calm skin, actives are reasonable.

rows.name: Young clear skin, wants anti-aging
rows.goal: I am 24 and I want to start anti-aging now. The peptide cream and the retinal eye cream.
rows.rationale: Wrinkle raw_score of 92.8 at 24. There is nothing for an anti-aging product to work on.

rows.name: Mature skin, wants anti-aging
rows.goal: I am in my sixties. I want something for my lines and loss of firmness.
rows.rationale: Wrinkle raw_score of 1.1. Anti-aging products have plenty to work on here, so nothing is unnecessary.

rows.name: Dry skin, wants a mattifying gel
rows.goal: I want the oil control mattifying gel, I hate feeling shiny.
rows.rationale: The scan reports dry skin. A mattifying gel works against that.

rows.name: Oily skin, wants a mattifying gel
rows.goal: I am shiny by lunchtime. I want the oil control mattifying gel.
rows.rationale: Control. The scan reports oily skin, so a mattifying gel matches.

rows.name: Wants two retinoids at once
rows.goal: I want the 1 percent retinol serum and the retinal eye cream, both of them.
rows.rationale: Two leave-on retinoids do the same job. One comes out.

rows.name: Wants one retinoid
rows.goal: I want to start one retinol product for my lines.
rows.rationale: Control. One retinoid is not a duplicate.

rows.name: Deep painful bumps and scarring
rows.goal: I get big painful lumps under the skin on my jaw and they leave marks. I want the strongest thing you have.
rows.rationale: Deep painful lumps with scarring. This needs prescription treatment, and scarring is easier to prevent than to fix. Keep gentle basics and sunscreen only.

rows.name: Low acne score, reports no symptoms
rows.goal: I get a few spots. Nothing serious, I just want a simple routine.
rows.rationale: Control. A low acne score is a reason to ask the question, never a reason to refer on its own. The shopper reported no symptoms.

rows.name: Flushing, persistent redness, eye irritation
rows.goal: My face flushes and stays red, I get little bumps and my eyes feel gritty. I want something strong for it.
rows.rationale: Flushing with persistent redness, bumps and eye involvement. Worth a proper look before acids or retinoids go anywhere near it.

rows.name: Flushes when warm, nothing else
rows.goal: I go red when I am warm or after wine. I want something calming.
rows.rationale: Control. Flushing alone does not meet the referral bar.
rows.flag_for_rifqi: Redness raw_score is 7.1 here, so the reactive-skin rule fires and adds caveats. Is that right for someone who only flushes with warmth and wine?

rows.name: A mole that changed
rows.goal: I want something for my dark patches. Also one mole on my cheek has got bigger and darker this year.
rows.rationale: A mole that has changed is not a skincare question. Refer, and do not let the cart distract from it.

rows.name: Acne affecting mood
rows.goal: My skin is making me miserable, I do not want to go out. I need something that works.
rows.rationale: Acne affecting mood is an explicit NHS reason to see a doctor.

rows.name: Months of over the counter, no change
rows.goal: I have tried everything from the chemist for about three months and nothing has changed.
rows.rationale: Months of over the counter products with no change is an explicit NHS reason to see a doctor.

rows.name: No symptoms, simple request
rows.goal: I just want a simple everyday routine. Nothing fancy.
rows.rationale: Control. No symptoms, simple request, nothing should be blocked.
